subject: FY25 School Budget Request
overview: The Medford School Committee approved a level-service FY25 budget request of $79,399,774 to be submitted to the mayor and City Council, rejecting proposed administrative and staff cuts after hours of public comment from students, staff, and parents. The committee also celebrated student achievements in CCSR, humanities, and CTE programs, approved CTE program expansions for MSBA consideration, and recommended co-locating the Curtis-Tufts School with the high school campus.

items.title: Consent Agenda
items.summary: Approved the consent agenda, including bills, payrolls, minutes, and a $3,000 Massachusetts Cultural Council grant, after severing and amending minutes to add a meeting recording link and strike student addresses for privacy.

items.title: Handbook Review and Schedule Policy
items.summary: Approved on first reading a three-phase annual handbook update and approval process established by the ad hoc subcommittee.

items.title: Co-Locating Curtis-Tufts School with High School Campus
items.summary: Approved the subcommittee recommendation to co-locate the Curtis-Tufts therapeutic program onto the main high school campus during the Medford High School rebuilding project, referring it to the MSBA subcommittee.

items.title: Superintendent's Updates
items.summary: Superintendent Edouard-Vincent introduced the evening's recognitions and addressed concerns regarding the arts, clarifying that performing arts programs are not being eliminated and that the theater arts reduction resulted from an unreplaced resignation.

items.title: CCSR Update and Student Recognition
items.summary: Recognized CCSR program accomplishments, including a river cleanup initiative and an elementary student project providing emergency whistles to postal workers.

items.title: Humanities Student Recognition
items.summary: Recognized students for achievements across various humanities programs and competitions, including writing contests, Model UN, Ethics Bowl, Mock Trial, and Geography Bee.

items.title: Medford High School Update and Survey Results
items.summary: Presented positive school climate survey trends, new core values, and CTE highlights, while the committee voted to direct that Principal Cabral receive the staffing needed to pilot an alternative high school program.

items.title: Career and Technical Education Program Expansion
items.summary: Approved a motion requesting that the School Building Committee explore CTE program expansions and proposed new programs as part of the MSBA feasibility study.

items.title: FY25 Budget Update, Public Comment, and School Committee Vote
items.summary: Following extensive public comment and a student petition protesting proposed staff, nursing, and performing arts cuts, the committee voted to submit a level-service FY25 budget request of $79,399,774 to the mayor and City Council, with Mayor Lungo-Koehn abstaining.

items.title: Condolences and Adjournment
items.summary: Observed a moment of silence for family members of school staff before adjourning.
